message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a modest long position: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), operating income of $123.2 billion, and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion, with gross margin improving to 46.2% from 44.1% on a fast-growing Services segment ($96.2 billion, +13%, at 73.9% gross margin). Net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly year over year, but that was driven by a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2 billion net tax charge related to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not by any deterioration in the business; the balance sheet remains strong with $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities, and the company returned $95.0 billion via buybacks plus $15.2 billion in dividends. Risks I weighed include the 8% Greater China sales decline, DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure, and supply-chain concentration, which is why I sized the position conservatively rather than aggressively. I placed one buy order for 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00, which filled at $223.00 — about $8,920, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily total, with the limit set essentially at the current market (last $222.70, ask $222.72) and funded entirely from existing cash ($50,000), so no money left the account. (Note: the filing text contained a couple of sections flagged and removed by the security screen as attempted AI instructions; I disregarded them and relied only on the financial statements and MD&A.)
